candidate is trailing in the previous round's polls abstain with
probability ∝ demobilization_factor × poll_influence.

may switch to their best viable alternative. Tracks convergence
(winner stable for 2 consecutive rounds) and strategic drift.

P(null | method) = error_base × candidate_factor × education_factor

more voters than simple ones (Plurality).

bullet voting (collapses Approval to Plurality for affected voters),
primacy effect (Krosnick 1991, first-listed candidate bonus).

Each voter observes the last `observation_window` votes and may follow
the public signal instead of their sincere preference with probability
`cascade_strength`. Bikhchandani, Hirshleifer, Welch (1992).

affiliation) instead of their sincere preferences. Compares method
robustness.

For each voting method, allocates `total_seats` proportionally via
D'Hondt then greedily picks the smallest ideologically-coherent
coalition that crosses `government_threshold * total_seats`.

Voters with longer locks amplify their votes (×0.1 at 0 days,
×6.0 at 224 days). Compares the conviction-weighted result with a
plain 1-token-1-vote baseline.

200.description: Conviction winner vs token winner + per-proposal stats + Gini tokens vs Gini conviction.

post.summary: Polkadot-style conviction voting: tokens × multiplier(lock_days)

post.description:
Voters update their ideology toward a network-weighted mean for
`deliberation_rounds` rounds, then vote. `network_type` echo_chamber
amplifies polarisation; bridge / complete reduce it.

200.description: Pre vs post-deliberation winner, opinion convergence rate, polarisation change, per-round trace.

post.summary: DeGroot opinion update across a network, then vote

post.description:
Distortion between the real electorate and the effective electorate
driven by differential turnout across demographic groups. The
`correct_for_turnout` flag toggles the turnout-correction model
on/off so the user can compare both.

200.description: Biased vs corrected winner, representation gap, demographic breakdown.

post.summary: Full population vs effective electorate via age × education gaps

post.description:
Each district elects its winner by FPTP from a locally biased
electorate. Aggregates to a national parliament under FPTP (sum of
district wins) vs D'Hondt proportional on national vote shares.

200.description: Per-district winners + national parliaments (FPTP and D'Hondt proportional) + distortion index.

post.summary: N districts with locally shifted ideology, FPTP vs proportional

post.description:
Isolates the effect of blank-vote rules on inter-method agreement
by running the same electorate twice (without and with blank).

200.description: Methods, agreement, and per-method winner deltas for the two runs.

post.summary: Same electorate, with vs without blank vote

post.description:
P(vote | election k) = max(engaged_voter_pct, 1 - k × fatigue_rate).
Engaged voters (top engaged_voter_pct by max-utility) always vote;
casual voters drop out faster each election, shifting the residual
electorate toward partisans.

200.description: Per-election turnout, winner, ideology drift, and a representation-gap measure of how much the residual electorate diverges from the full population.

post.summary: Turnout decay across repeated elections

post.description:
Voters assigned to the (smallest) overlapping district or the
nearest one. Compares the gerrymandered FPTP parliament to a
D'Hondt proportional reference.

200.description: Per-district winners + gerrymander parliament + proportional reference + gerrymander index.

post.summary: Voters assigned to user-drawn rectangular districts

post.description:
Brownian campaign simulation for 4 historical scenarios
(France 2002, USA 1992, Germany 2021, Condorcet cycle). Drag a
candidate's x/y position to rewrite history.

200.description: Per-day winners (FPTP/Condorcet/Borda), scenario metadata, and a pedagogical note on divergence from the real winner.

post.summary: Day-by-day historical replay with candidate-position overrides

post.description:
Each candidate iteratively moves in the direction (±x, ±y) that
maximises their vote score under `method`. Converges when no
candidate can improve by moving by `step_size`.

200.description: Iteration-by-iteration candidate positions, convergence status, equilibrium type.

post.summary: Hotelling-Downs iterative best-response (Nash equilibrium)

post.description:
Pure rule-based text interpretation of an existing /simulate
response. No new simulation.

200.description: Headline + Condorcet analysis + divergence reason + per-winner method groups + pedagogical note + key facts.

post.summary: Deterministic interpretation of a /simulate result

post.description:
The bundling problem: a platform can win the election while the majority
disagrees with it issue by issue (Ostrogorski / discursive dilemma).
Spatial mode derives K issues from the shared electorate; handcrafted mode
builds exact paradoxes.

200.description: Per-issue referendum majorities, the elected platform, divergences, and the Ostrogorski-paradox flag.

post.summary: Issue-by-issue majorities vs the bundled platform vote

post.description:
Voters with individual competence p > 0.5 aggregate collectively
toward the 'correct' option. Runs `num_simulations` Monte Carlo
trials and compares plurality, IRV, Borda, Schulze, MJ on the same
juries.

200.description: Per-method accuracy, theoretical majority-rule accuracy, and a competence-curve sensitivity chart.

post.summary: Condorcet Jury Theorem under N voting methods

post.description:
Each voter votes directly or delegates. Delegation chains are
resolved up to `max_chain_length` hops; cycles fall back to direct
voting. Reports voting-weight Gini and a super-voter list.

200.description: Weighted tallies + super-voter list + delegation graph + Gini curve of voting weight.

post.summary: Transitive delegation up to max_chain_length hops

post.description:
Same electorate, 5 multi-winner methods. Reports per-method
seat allocation, distortion against the proportional reference,
and which method comes closest to / furthest from proportional.

200.description: Per-method seats + distortion vs proportional + best/worst methods.

post.summary: STV / D'Hondt / SPAV / Phragmén / FPTP on the same electorate

post.description:
A voter casts NOTA when their max-utility for any candidate is below
nota_threshold. Three constitutional outcomes after NOTA wins:
`invalidate` (null election), `runoff` (new candidates), or
`winner_take_all` (seat NOTA, Nevada-style).

200.description: Sincere winner, NOTA percentage, election validity per the constitutional rule, NOTA-vs-threshold curve, and a per-method comparison of NOTA inclusiveness.

post.summary: NOTA (None Of The Above) as a ballot option

post.description:
Parties adapt positions (Hotelling), get eliminated below
`survival_threshold`, and new parties may emerge. Tactical voting
squeezes small parties under FPTP, driving the system toward
bipartism.

200.description: Per-election parties, effective parties curve, final system (bipartite vs multipartite), convergence speed.

post.summary: Multi-election party-system evolution (Duverger's Law)

post.description:
For each voter distribution in `ideology_range`, computes the
Esteban-Ray polarisation index and runs `num_simulations` Monte
Carlo elections to measure how method agreement and Condorcet
rate degrade with polarisation.

200.description: One result per ideology distribution: ER index, Condorcet rate, inter-method agreement, regret by method.

post.summary: Per-ideology Esteban-Ray index + voting-method robustness

post.description:
Shapley-Shubik (pivot-in-permutation) and Banzhaf

200.description: Per-party Shapley + Banzhaf indices + power ratio + viable coalitions + power-surprise list.

post.summary: Shapley-Shubik and Banzhaf power indices for coalition bargaining

post.description:
Each party holds an internal primary among its partisan voters;
the primary winner runs in the general election. The
`without_primaries_winner` field reports what would have happened

conclusions are conditional on the assumptions.

post.description:
Enumerates all `n!` agendas for `n` alternatives and reports which
outcomes the agenda-setter can engineer. A consequence of Plott's
Chaos Theorem when no Condorcet winner exists.

200.description: Pairwise matrix + Condorcet winner + every achievable outcome over all agenda permutations + manipulation power.

post.summary: McKelvey-style agenda manipulation under binary elimination

post.description:
Hamilton + 4 divisor methods (Jefferson, Webster, Adams,
Huntington-Hill) with quota-violation / Alabama / population
paradox detection. Demonstrates Balinski-Young (1982): no method
avoids all three paradoxes.

200.description: Per-method seat allocation + paradox flags + Balinski-Young summary.

post.summary: Apportionment methods + Balinski-Young impossibility

post.description:
For each of single_peaked / stable_preferences / rational_voters /
fixed_electorate / measurable_utilities, relaxes the assumption
and measures how often the winner changes vs the baseline. Reports
which assumption the result depends on most.

200.description: Per-assumption Monte-Carlo result + most fragile assumption + overall robustness flag.

post.summary: Test spatial-model robustness by relaxing core assumptions

post.description:
Same electorate, many methods, many binary-agenda orderings.
Counts how many distinct winners emerge. A high count supports
Schumpeter's procedural view; a low count supports Rousseau's
general-will view. Cross-checks against the Condorcet winner.

200.description: Per-method + per-agenda winners + Rousseau score (=1 iff all procedures agree) + Condorcet check + philosophical conclusion.

post.summary: Does the general will exist, or is it a procedural artefact?

post.description:
Models gerrymandering / media-capture / voter-suppression
compounding across elections. Optional guardrails (constitutional
court, free press, international pressure, supermajority lock-in)
slow the decay.

200.description: Per-election state (vote shares, democratic quality, guardrails triggered) + autocracy detection + tipping points.

post.summary: Path toward autocracy across successive elections

post.description:
Compares 4 weighting schemes: equal democracy, competence-weighted
voting, epistocratic (threshold-gated), and lottery. Models Caplan's
4 systematic biases as a competence reduction. Reports the
democracy-vs-expert tradeoff.

200.description: Per-scheme Bayesian regret + correct-choice rate + voter competence stats + democracy-vs-expert delta.

post.summary: Epistocratic voting vs standard democracy (Caplan / Brennan)

post.description:
Models the empirical pattern where voters adopt their camp's
positions instead of choosing camps from their positions. The
`identity_weight` parameter sweeps from pure ideological voting
(0.0) to pure identity voting (1.0).

200.description: Sincere vs identity vs mixed winners + per-group loyalty / ideology match + cross-pressured abstention + identity-weight sweep curve.

post.summary: Green/Palmquist/Schickler 2002 identity-based voting

post.description:
Monte-Carlo simulation: for each n, generate `num_trials` random
profiles, run plurality on the full profile then on the profile
with one random candidate removed, count winner changes. Other
methods are scaled from the plurality baseline.

200.description: Curve of (n_candidates, violation_rate) for n in [2, max_candidates].

post.summary: Empirical IIA violation rate vs number of candidates

post.description:
How institutional representation of future generations changes the
adoption rate of decisions whose costs are present and benefits
are future. Rawls' veil-of-ignorance heuristic.

200.description: Per-decision outcome under 4 mechanisms (none / proxy / age_weighted / veto) + cross-mechanism aggregates.

post.summary: Future-generation representation in long-horizon decisions

post.description:
Majority rule on propositions can produce collectively incoherent
results even when every individual voter is perfectly coherent.
Pre-defined scenarios: legal liability, fiscal trilemma, climate.

200.description: Per-proposition collective vote + coherence diagnosis + premise-based vs conclusion-based resolution.

post.summary: Discursive dilemma (List & Pettit 2002)

post.description:
Same electorate, 6 decision rules (simple majority, 2/3 + 3/4
supermajorities, unanimous, QV, MJ). Measures how often a fixed
majority can override a high-intensity minority.

200.description: Per-rule minority-protection metrics + tyranny curve (majority share 0.51 -> 0.80) + best/worst rule.

post.summary: Tocqueville's tyranny of the majority across decision rules

post.description:
For each voter, tests four manipulation strategies (compromising,
burying, pushover, truncating) and keeps the one with the highest
utility gain. Empirical demonstration of Gibbard-Satterthwaite.

200.description: Per-voter best manipulation (strategy + utility gain) + key manipulator + pedagogical note.

post.summary: Gibbard-Satterthwaite manipulator identification

post.description:
In ≥2-D policy space with ≥3 voters, a Condorcet winner almost
never exists, and from any starting point the agenda-setter can
reach ANY other point via a sequence of majority votes.

200.description: Condorcet-winner flag, top cycle (Smith set), and two BFS paths showing the agenda-setter can reach diametrically opposite outcomes from the same start.

post.summary: Plott's Chaos Theorem in 2-D policy space

post.description:
Sen 1970: no social choice rule satisfies Pareto efficiency AND
minimal individual liberalism simultaneously. Tests the canonical
case and samples random preference profiles to estimate paradox
frequency.

200.description: Canonical Lady-Chatterley example + random profiles + resolution options.

post.summary: Sen's Impossibility of a Paretian Liberal (1970)
